Hi everyone! My name is Corijn and I'm a PhD student in number theory at the LSGNT in London. I've been looking at Lean and Mathlib for a few years, but now I've finally convinced myself to start an actual project and join the community.

My first idea for a basic starter project was to formalise a lemma on pointed sets relevant to my thesis. However, for this I would like to use basic facts and definitions about pointed sets, such as kernels and images of morphisms that should again be pointed sets, and I don't think Mathlib currently has these things (but please let me know if it does!). It seems to me that the current implementation of pointed sets in Mathlib is in the file CategoryTheory/Category/Pointed.lean. This contains definitions of the objects and morphisms in the category of pointed sets, but not that much else. So, to do my lemma, I would first need to flesh out the category of pointed sets a bit. I would not mind actually to change my project from proving the lemma to just working on the category of pointed sets in Lean. Would that be a welcome contribution to Mathlib?

If yes, I can think of two slightly different paths I could take:

  • I could simply add exactly the things I need for the lemma to the current Pointed.lean file. Maybe I could even slightly improve the current code, for example by changing the instance declarations of FunLike and ConcreteCategory to use Pointed.Hom instead of an anonymous subtype?
  • Another option would be to work on the category of pointed sets more properly in the style of the categories of other algebraic structures like monoids and groups. For example, it could go in a directory Algebra/Category/PointedCat and I could start with Basic.lean and Limits.lean files, exactly following the example of Algebra/Category/MonCat. This would probably be much more work, but perhaps also more useful to Mathlib?

Could either of these options be a good project? I would also be very interested to hear if anyone is already working with pointed sets in Lean!

Thanks in advance!
Welcome! Given that @Edison Xie was around to help out last week, he might be interested in this.

I think probably you should develop more about Pointed (e.g id_comp and comp_id) before going into the category world and make a separate higher priority ext lemma, changing the FunLike instance, etc.
in general I think it would be good to develop the concrete part as much as you could and you then convert to the category world but make everything transparent
Hi Edison, thanks for the advice! In that case I will first just try to add some things like kernels to Pointed.

Is there scope / interest in generalising this to the "category of pointed objects"? which is equivalently docs#CategoryTheory.Under applied to (a / the) terminal object — a cursory look around seems to suggest a lot of the theory of pointed sets generalises to this setting (though I completely understand if diving into the the full generality is a bit much for a first project)

even (imo — disclaimer i am not familiar with mathlib's category theory library) proving a lemma saying Pointed is isomorphic / equivalent to Under PUnit could be neat

EDIT (i'm procrastinating) i came up with the following (i don't mean to hijack your intro thread! i'm happy to take further discussion if any to a new forum)

Pointed and Under PUnit are equivalent

import Mathlib.CategoryTheory.Comma.Over.Basic
import Mathlib.CategoryTheory.Category.Pointed

universe u

namespace CategoryTheory

open Pointed Under ConcreteCategory TypeCat

def underPUnitToPointed : Under PUnit.{u+1} ⥤ Pointed.{u} where
  obj f := of (X := f.right) (f.hom.hom.toFun .unit)
  map φ := ⟨φ.right.hom.toFun, congr_hom (Under.w φ) .unit⟩

def pointedToUnderPUnit : Pointed.{u} ⥤ Under PUnit.{u+1} where
  obj α := mk (ofHom fun _ => α.point)
  map f := homMk (ofHom f.toFun) <| by ext; exact f.map_point

def underPUnitPointedEquiv : Under PUnit.{u+1} ≌ Pointed.{u} where
  functor := underPUnitToPointed
  inverse := pointedToUnderPUnit
  unitIso := Iso.refl _
  counitIso := Iso.refl _

end CategoryTheory

Hi Thomas, thanks for your reply! I'm no expert on these things so please correct me if I'm wrong. If I understand correctly a category of pointed objects is exactly a pointed category, so a category with a zero object. You're probably right that many things one could prove for the category of pointed sets would also work for any category with a zero object.

Personally, I would be happy to just work with pointed sets because there at least I am very sure about the mathematics and I can focus on understanding the Lean. But please don't let me stop you from doing something in higher generality!

I like your equivalence with Under PUnit, it is helpful to see how such a construction works in Lean :)

of course! & that sounds absolutely the right option :)

on the pointed category idea, certainly Under T for T a terminal object is pointed, with zero object the identity 𝟙 T : T ⟶ T — i'd have to think further to see whether there is an equivalence the other way. in any case, i think with some pushing & pulling the existence of kernels (indeed all limits and colimits) follows from general results, but if pointed sets are what you're interested i would guess that's more trouble than it's worth.

either way all the best for your lean adventures!

If CCC is a category with zero object ooo, then CCC is isomorphic to the under category o↓Co \downarrow Co↓C. I'm not sure about general limits, but for kernels perhaps what you want is already in Mathlib? Because to show that a category is an instance of CategoryTheory.Limits.HasKernels, all you need is that the category HasZeroMorphisms (which follows from the existence of a zero object).

Thanks!
right! by the results i linked above limits and colimits lift from C to Under A for any A : C, but i suppose for Pointed you'd want a more explicit description
